text.p: Britain's National Westminster Bank Plc, which has been the subject of merger speculation, said on Tuesday it had an independent future and ruled out significant acquisitions.

Asked if this also ruled out mergers, NatWest chairman Lord Alexander told reporters, "We have a strong, robust independent future and we are clear that we have the ability to improve through our own organic efforts. We do not need a partner."
Earlier NatWest's chief executive Derek Wanless told Reuters the group's troubled investment banking arm NatWest Markets was not for sale.
Alexander said the speculation about NatWest in recent months had been overblown and that talks with two institutions, which he declined to name, had not got as far as the press had speculated.
"They were exploratory talks and never got anywhere near talking about jobs," Alexander said.

The press has speculated that talks with Abbey National and Prudential Corporation on a possible merger broke down partly because no agreement could be reached on which executives would run the business.

Asked if it would make sense for NatWest to buy an insurance company to boost its capability in long-term savings and pensions, Wanless said: "Yes it could make strategic sense but it becomes a question of value for shareholders. We can't justify it on those grounds so we won't be doing it."

Wanless said one acquisition the bank still wanted to make was TSB Ireland which he said was dependent on when the Irish government was ready to sell. He said this would make a good addition to NatWest unit Ulster Bank but did not expect any near-term movement from the Irish authorities.
